description: Demonstrates every Journey Runner tool and capability: command execution, DOM interaction (click, input), visual annotations (highlight, screenshot, notice), ribbon button interaction with highlight, theme switching, event system (emit, assert), navigation, eval with variable passing, wait timing, manual QA documentation, lifecycle tools (create-file, delete-file, open-file, open-url, close-leaves, close-modals, seed), and WebViewer content interaction via Electron webview.executeJavaScript(). Uses vault file creation as a concrete scenario, ribbon navigation, and the Obsidian Help page to exercise each tool in a realistic context.

steps.title: WebViewer: open URL and interact with content
steps.description: Demonstrates: open-url, eval (webview detection + webview.executeJavaScript for cross-process content interaction), highlight (DOM + webview target), screenshot, close via eval, wait. Opens a URL in Obsidian's built-in WebViewer, verifies the webview element, highlights content inside the isolated webview DOM, reads page content via executeJavaScript, and closes the viewer.

interactions: eval: Read page title via executeJavaScript

Open the Obsidian Help page via CLI 'web' command

actions.code: (() => { const wv = document.querySelector('webview'); if (wv) return 'found'; throw new Error('No <webview> element found in DOM'); })()
actions.description: Verify a <webview> element exists in the Obsidian DOM
Highlight the WebViewer tab title (DOM highlight)

Highlight the main heading inside the webview content (cross-process highlight)

actions.description: Webview content with heading highlighted via cross-process injection

actions.code: (async () => { const wv = document.querySelector('webview'); const title = await wv.executeJavaScript('document.title'); return title || 'no-title'; })()
actions.description: Read page title from inside webview via executeJavaScript (cross-process interaction)
Show the page title read from webview content

actions.code: (() => { let closed = 0; app.workspace.iterateAllLeaves(l => { if (l.view?.containerEl?.querySelector('webview')) { l.detach(); closed++; } }); return String(closed); })()
actions.description: Close all leaves containing a <webview> element

actions.instruction: Verify: (1) webviewer-open shows the Obsidian Help page loaded with the tab title highlighted in green (DOM highlight). (2) webviewer-content-highlight shows a cyan highlight on the main heading inside the webview — this proves cross-process DOM highlighting works via webview injection. (3) The notice shows the page title read via webview.executeJavaScript(), proving cross-process content interaction. All three WebViewer capabilities (open-url, webview highlight, executeJavaScript) are demonstrated in a single step.
actions.description: WebViewer open-url, highlight, and content interaction QA
